verdicts.claim: A checkpoint copies committed WAL frames into the main database file. When several frames hold versions of the same page, only the newe
verdicts.evidence: Fly.io: checkpointing "copies the latest version of each page in the WAL back into the main database file"

verdicts.claim: A checkpoint runs concurrently with readers but must stop at the first WAL frame past the end mark of any active reader
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "the checkpoint must stop when it reaches a page in the WAL that is past the end mark of any current reader"

verdicts.claim: The WAL is reset, not truncated, by default: once every frame has been checkpointed ... the next writer rewinds to the start
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "the writer will rewind the WAL back to the beginning"; Fly.io: checkpoint sequence number "gets incremented on each checkpoint". New-salt detail not stated verbatim in fetched summaries.

verdicts.claim: Automatic checkpoints are PASSIVE and run inside the committing connection, in the committing thread ... default is 1000 pages
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "checkpoint will be run automatically by the same thread that does the COMMIT"; pragma: "interval of 1000 or SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT"; c3ref: "Checkpoints initiated by this mechanism are PASSIVE"

verdicts.claim: sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2() and PRAGMA wal_checkpoint accept five modes ... NOOP, added in SQLite 3.51.0
verdicts.evidence: c3ref lists PASSIVE/FULL/RESTART/TRUNCATE/NOOP; release log under 3.51.0: "Add the PRAGMA wal_checkpoint=NOOP; command and the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP argument"

verdicts.claim: FULL, RESTART and TRUNCATE take the exclusive writer lock and invoke the busy handler ... block new writers ... new readers proceed
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: "blocks new database writers while it is pending" and "new database readers are allowed to continue unimpeded"

verdicts.claim: Every checkpoint call first takes an exclusive checkpoint lock. If another connection already holds it, the call returns SQLITE_BUSY
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: "All calls obtain an exclusive 'checkpoint' lock"; busy handler "will not be invoked in this case"

verdicts.claim: PRAGMA journal_size_limit (default -1, no limit) truncates the -wal file ... Syncthing saw TRUNCATE shrink the WAL to zero bytes despite 67108864
verdicts.evidence: pragma: "default journal size limit is -1 (no limit)"; calmh: "truncates back to zero bytes, regardless of our PRAGMA journal_size_limit = 67108864" ... "connection pooling issues were the cause"

verdicts.claim: sqlite3_wal_hook() registers a callback invoked after each WAL-mode commit with the connection, the database name and page count
verdicts.evidence: wal_hook: callback "may read, write or checkpoint"; error "will propagate back up"; autocheckpoint "is a wrapper around sqlite3_wal_hook()". 'Intended way' wording not in source.

verdicts.claim: Litestream holds a long-running read transaction between its own checkpoints ... recommends wal_autocheckpoint=0 plus busy_timeout=5000
verdicts.evidence: how-it-works: "starts a long-running read transaction"; tips: "tens of thousands per second", "takes a fresh full snapshot", "Checkpoint detection improvements in v0.5.0+"

verdicts.claim: Practical hardening: upgrade to SQLite 3.51.3 or later; disable auto-checkpoint ...; run PRAGMA integrity_check on backups continuously
verdicts.evidence: Tailscale fetch redirected (303) off-site; Litestream tips only advises integrity_check after restore, not continuous backup checks.

verdicts.claim: With PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL in WAL mode the checkpoint is the only sync point ... EXTRA is identical to FULL in WAL mode
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "with PRAGMA synchronous set to NORMAL, the checkpoint is the only operation to issue an I/O barrier or sync operation"; pragma: "EXTRA is no different from FULL in WAL mode"

verdicts.claim: Checkpoints cost more than write transactions ... read performance falls as the WAL grows ... dedicated thread, process or service
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "read performance deteriorates as the WAL file grows"; PhotoStructure: "Consider dedicated maintenance process"

verdicts.claim: After VACUUM in WAL mode, run PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) ... journal_size_limit does not limit WAL growth during the VACUUM
verdicts.evidence: PhotoStructure: journal_size_limit "does NOT prevent WAL growth during VACUUM"; recommends PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)

verdicts.claim: Checkpoint starvation: if overlapping read transactions ensure there is always at least one active reader ... grows without bound
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound"

verdicts.claim: VACUUM in WAL mode ... nearly doubling disk use ... Since SQLite 3.11.0 (2016-02-15) a transaction's WAL footprint is proportional
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "Beginning with version 3.11.0 (2016-02-15), WAL mode works as efficiently with large transactions"; PhotoStructure: "you almost double disk consumption"

verdicts.claim: PRAGMA wal_checkpoint returns one row with three columns: busy, log, checkpointed ... -1 if not WAL ... After TRUNCATE both counts are 0
verdicts.evidence: pragma: "The second and third column are -1 if there is no write-ahead log"; Syncthing calmh ignored return values. 'Both counts 0 after TRUNCATE' not stated verbatim.

verdicts.claim: A single prepared SELECT stepped to a row but not reset keeps its read transaction open ... reproducer on SQLite 3.30.0 and 3.38.5
verdicts.evidence: Forum: tested against 3.30.0 and 3.38.5; prevention "will keep the WAL file around the desired 4 MB / 1000 pages"

verdicts.claim: Syncthing's SQLite backend ran PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) every 8 hours with a 64 MiB journal_size_limit ...
verdicts.evidence: Syncthing thread: "currently 64 MiB in our code ... Currently we do that every 8h"; 26121 lists long transactions, truncation needs no readers, "We don't disable the auto checkpoint". Proposal to disable auto-checkpoint is implied, not explicit.

verdicts.claim: The WAL-reset bug ... likely present from 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09); fixed in 3.51.3 (2026-03-13) with backports
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "likely present in all version of SQLite from 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09)" ... "fixed in version 3.51.3 (2026-03-13)"; backports link 3.44.6/3.50.7. 3.52.0 withdrawal confirmed only via sqlite.org news (not cited).

verdicts.claim: SQLite describes the WAL-reset race as unlikely in common use and says its developers never reproduced it organically, only with a test hook
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "unlikely to occur in common use"; "unable to reproduce the bug organically"

verdicts.claim: Antithesis reproduced it on 3.51.2 in about 15 minutes with a generic workload of concurrent writes and checkpoints; clean on 3.51.3
verdicts.evidence: Antithesis: "caught the bug in 15 mins"; "just runs writes and checkpoints concurrently"; "3.51.3 comes back clean" (2026-08-12)

verdicts.claim: Tailscale recorded 19 corruption incidents over about six months from August 2025 with a single Go process per shard ... four months without incidents
verdicts.evidence: Cited page fetch redirected (303) off-site; secondary coverage (techzine, search summary) agrees on 19 incidents, ~six months, aggressive manual checkpointing, four months clean; 'single Go process per shard' unconfirmed.

verdicts.claim: Disagreement: Fly.io says SQLite 'will not force a checkpoint on its own'; Litestream says SQLite can only checkpoint when no transactions are active
verdicts.evidence: Fly.io: "SQLite will not force a checkpoint on its own" and "block new read & write transactions"; Litestream: checkpointing "can only be done when no transactions are active"
